text: dsh-pdf-reader（DSH 桌面插件）：在本地检查、读取、搜索和查看 PDF 页面。它通过 Harness 工具接口提供 PDF 状态检查、页面检查、带引用的文本读取、文字搜索，以及整页或局部图像渲染；对文字稀少或含嵌入图像的页面可选择性使用本地 OCR。适合需要从 PDF 中提取文字、定位内容并核对图表的 DSH 用户。读取和转换依赖系统安装的 Poppler；OCR 还需要 Tesseract 及相应语言数据。

dsh-pdf-reader adds DSH tools to inspect PDF pages, read cited text, search embedded text, and render a page or crop as an image. Sparse pages can use local OCR. It requires Poppler, and OCR also requires Tesseract with language data.
想在 DSH 里按页读取 PDF，并保留页码引用。
能不能从扫描版 PDF 中识别文字？
我需要搜索 PDF 正文并找到匹配页码。
让 DSH 把 PDF 页面或图表裁剪后显示出来。
想检查 PDF 哪些页面缺少可提取的文字。
读取表格 PDF 时怎样尽量保留行列间距？
I need page-cited text extraction from PDFs in DSH.
Can DSH OCR scanned PDF pages locally?
dsh-pdf-reader 的功能「分页面读取」：读取指定 PDF 页并返回页码引用，支持最多 10 页一批、近似保留表格布局和文本续读偏移；可选择自动、关闭或强制本地 OCR。
dsh-pdf-reader 的功能「正文搜索」：按字面内容搜索 PDF 的可提取文本，返回匹配片段和物理页码引用，并报告稀疏文本页及继续取回结果所需的偏移。
dsh-pdf-reader 的功能「页面检查」：查看 PDF 页数、各页文字量和嵌入图像数量，标记可能需要 OCR 检查的页面，并提供分页继续字段。
dsh-pdf-reader 的功能「页面渲染」：把指定 PDF 页或按比例选取的裁剪区域渲染成图像附件，供当前支持图像输入的模型查看。

dsh-pdf-reader README · DSH PDF Reader：A standalone DeepSeek Harness plugin for reading PDFs in DSH Desktop. No desktop shell modifications, npm runtime dependencies, background indexing or model downloads.

dsh-pdf-reader README · What it does：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `pdf_status` | Check Poppler, Tesseract and installed OCR languages. |
| `pdf_inspect` | Page count, page-level text availability, scan warnings and coverage. |
| `pdf_read` | Read page ranges, preserve table spacing, selectively OCR scans, and report truncation. |
| `pdf_search` | Literal search of embedded text with page references and explicit scan coverage gaps. |
| `pdf_render` | Send a whole page or magnified crop as a real Harness image attachment. |

dsh-pdf-reader README · What it does：Attach a PDF normally and ask:

> Use the PDF tools to read this document. Inspect its pages first, OCR scanned pages in English and Chinese, and inspect relevant figures. Explain the findings with PDF page references. Tell me which pages or regions you could not read.

For a specific table:

> Read PDF page 6 with layout preserved, then render a crop of the table and check the numbers against the text. Cite the page.

dsh-pdf-reader README · What it does：The plugin adds a short reading workflow to the agent's system prompt. The current agent preset must allow these tools. If a restricted preset hides them, use a preset that permits plugin tools.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Compatibility：This is a **Harness host plugin**, with no dependency on Tauri, Electron internals, or a custom desktop fork. It uses the official tool registry, filesystem, system-prompt and attachment services.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Compatibility：| Host | Status |
| --- | --- |
| DSH Tauri Desktop on Linux, Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` | Installed, enabled and observed running; integration and OCR tests passed. |
| Native macOS plugin execution | The 0.1.1 packed plugin passed all 22 integration tests with Node 24, Poppler and Tesseract in GitHub Actions. |
| Official DeepSeek Harness Desktop | Uses the same plugin mechanism. The official source reviewed on 2026-10-02 is also `0.2.0-rc.2`. Compatibility is expected when the required services and native dependencies are present; the packaged official desktop has not been tested here. |
| Harness `0.2.1-alpha.1` / `0.2.1-alpha.2` / `0.2.1-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.5` / `0.2.2-alpha.2` on Linux | Packed plugin tests pass in CI. |
| Other Harness versions or Windows | Not yet validated. |

dsh-pdf-reader README · Compatibility：The official desktop is described in [DeepSeek's desktop documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/desktop/README.md). Its runtime follows the desktop release, so check the installed version rather than assuming every desktop contains the latest runtime. The consumer DeepSeek chat website/app is a separate product and does not load this Harness plugin.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Compatibility：Poppler and Tesseract are external native programs: this package does not bundle them. Install versions matching the host OS and architecture. GUI applications may have a different PATH from your terminal; configure absolute paths if `pdf_status` reports missing tools. On Apple Silicon Homebrew commonly installs binaries under `/opt/homebrew/bin`; on Intel Macs under `/usr/local/bin`. Windows requires its own native executables and OCR language data; the Linux OCR wrapper is not portable.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Installation：Requires Node 22.19+ or 24+ and DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` or newer with the tool output, filesystem and attachment interfaces. The package declares this Harness floor so plugin managers can check it before installation. Tested against Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` on Linux. The packaged official desktop GUI and Windows execution have not been tested.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Installation：Download `dsh-pdf-reader-0.1.5.tgz` from the [GitHub release](https://github.com/SkanderBog/dsh-pdf-reader/releases/tag/v0.1.5). Use the desktop's Plugins page to install the archive and enable **dsh-pdf-reader**. This project is distributed through GitHub releases. The unscoped `dsh-pdf-reader` name on npm belongs to a different author; use this repository's archive or GitHub source to install this plugin.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Installation：For the official desktop, prefer its Plugins page. If using the command installed by the official desktop, launch the desktop once to initialize its profile, fully quit it, then run:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/dsh-pdf-reader-0.1.5.tgz
```

Reopen the desktop after the command finishes. Do not use `desktop` as the profile for a community shell unless that shell actually owns that profile. Restart the Harness core if its profile does not use hot reload.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Installation：For a named CLI profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile YOUR_PROFILE add /absolute/path/dsh-pdf-reader-0.1.5.tgz
```

Use the profile that the desktop actually runs; its name is not necessarily `web` or `desktop`. Package installation and bundle activation are managed by Harness. Do not copy tool code into the model provider or edit the desktop's generated frontend.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Installation：To disable or uninstall, use that same plugin manager. Disabling removes the tools and workflow; in-memory coverage and temporary working PDFs are discarded. Generated image attachments already in a conversation remain managed by Harness.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Store compatibility and permissions：`engines.dsh` is the host's version gate. DSH STORE separately reads `dsh.compatibility.dsh`, `dshReleases` and `dshOperations`; the manifest declares both formats. Packed API tests pass on DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.1-alpha.2`, `0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.5`, and `0.2.2-alpha.2`. The compatibility matrix describes tested host APIs, not every desktop GUI or OS. Installation/start/uninstall have separate disposable CLI-profile evidence for `0.2.0-rc.2` and current `0.2.1-rc.5`; update rollback remains unknown.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Store compatibility and permissions：| Capability | Scope and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Source files | Read through the mounted Harness filesystem service; access is checked on each invocation. Source PDFs are never modified. |
| Local writes | Private OS temporary document/OCR files; rendered images are stored through the host attachment service. Unload removes working copies; a hard crash may leave OS temporary files. |
| Commands | Poppler and Tesseract only, using fixed argument arrays with `shell: false`, cancellation, deadlines and output limits. An administrator may configure absolute executable paths; those binaries must be trusted. |
| Network | No direct plugin network requests. Harness may send returned PDF text/images to the conversation's selected model provider. |
| Environment / credentials | Native subprocesses receive an explicit runtime-path/font/OCR allowlist rather than the full host environment. API keys, tokens, proxy authentication, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `LD_PRELOAD`, and dynamic-library search overrides (`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH`) are not forwarded. The plugin does not request a credential service

dsh-pdf-reader README · Store compatibility and permissions：See [the store review evidence](validation/STORE-1336.md) for the exact scanner findings, reproduction commands and remaining admission boundary. File/command access is essential to a local PDF processor; Store's October 15 review keeps installation blocked pending independent verification of the native dependencies. These declarations do not grant store approval or independent security certification.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Native dependencies：Poppler supplies `pdfinfo`, `pdftotext`, `pdfimages` and `pdftoppm`. Tesseract is needed for local OCR; image rendering and selectable text do not require it.

Ubuntu/Debian:

```sh
sudo apt install poppler-utils tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng tesseract-ocr-chi-sim
```

macOS (native tools tested in CI; packaged desktop GUI not validated here):

```sh
brew install poppler tesseract tesseract-lang
```

dsh-pdf-reader README · Native dependencies：Each binary can be configured with an absolute executable path in the plugin's Cordis `config`, for example `tesseract: /absolute/path/tesseract`. Default names resolve through the desktop process's PATH. A user-local Tesseract wrapper at `~/.local/share/dsh-pdf-reader/tesseract` is detected automatically. That optional runtime is installed separately; it is not bundled into the npm package.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Native dependencies：The executable, its shared libraries, and its font/OCR configuration must come from sources you trust. An absolute path identifies a program but does not authenticate it. The plugin retains `PATH`, home directories, and font/OCR settings for native compatibility; it does not verify their ownership or prevent a trusted wrapper from setting its own environment. Custom installations needing private libraries must set a fixed library path inside their reviewed wrapper instead of relying on an inherited `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or `DYLD_*` value.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Native dependencies：For a reproducible local dependency inventory, run `node scripts/native-evidence.mjs > ../native-evidence.json` from the source checkout. Pass explicit paths matching your Cordis configuration, for example `--tesseract /absolute/path/tesseract`. The script hashes the plugin runtime and resolved native executables, probes their versions with the plugin's filtered environment, and records environment variable names only. Review the programs before running this command: version probes execute them. This inventory is author evidence, not Store approval or a signature check; wrappers, shared libraries, configuration and OCR data need separate source verification. See [the Store review evidence](validation/STORE-1336.md).

dsh-pdf-reader README · Native dependencies：The OCR language defaults to `eng`. Ask the agent to pass `language: "eng+chi_sim"` for English and Simplified Chinese. `pdf_status` lists languages actually installed. Other languages need their matching Tesseract data.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Design and limits：- Source bytes are read through the mounted Harness filesystem provider, with the calling session's working directory. Access is rechecked on every tool call, even for cached documents. Source files are never modified.
- Parsing and OCR run locally in temporary working copies using fixed executable arguments, no shell interpolation. The plugin itself makes no network calls. Extracted text and rendered images are subsequently sent to the conversation's configured model provider by Harness as normal tool results.
- The subprocess wrapper enforces deadlines, output limits, cancellation, and one OCR thread. On Linux and macOS, cancellation also terminates descendants of configured native wrappers in their process group. Cancelled queued tool calls return immediately without waiting for unrelated document processing. The child environment retains only runtime path, font and OCR settings (see `nativeEnvironment` in `src/process.mjs`). Custom wrappers that depend on other environment variables must set those values in the trusted wrapper itself. Tool processing is serialized to limit RAM use. At most four documents are cached; unloading the plugin

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The November 2 compatibility checks cover current Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` (also pinned by community Desktop `v0.30.0`) and upcoming `0.2.2-alpha.2`. The alpha host supplies its native tool executor; this plugin registers the same capabilities with both execution APIs. No desktop-shell implementation is required by the plugin.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The current DeepSeek adapter catalog reports Flash as image-capable and Pro as text-only. PDF rendering consults the routed provider's current metadata on every call, including configured model IDs and changed capabilities. Undisclosed metadata is reported as unknown. No model-name allowlist, automatic route switch, or paid generation is used by the compatibility probe. Account catalogs may differ; the live host metadata remains authoritative.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：With the relevant Harness model adapter installed in an isolated test runtime, run `node scripts/check-models.mjs RUNTIME_ROOT [PLUGIN_ENTRY]`. It checks twelve real registry/adapter cases, rendering actual images and reading embedded text, while refusing all network, authentication and model-generation attempts. The current-version CI lanes run it against the extracted archive. It does not assess remote answer accuracy.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The 2026-10-08 compatibility audit exercised this checkout alongside Context Manager, Rewind `0.15.0`, Better Sidebar `0.24.1` and DSH Market `1.66.6` in an isolated Harness `0.2.0-rc.2` host. Text extraction and image attachments worked through the shared tool registry; disabling the two audited plugins preserved the other plugins' registrations. Market coverage was limited to route registration and its read-only capabilities endpoint. The companion Context Manager repository contains the reproducible `test:installed` harness. Desktop `0.22.4` pins these same host APIs; its packaged GUI and all bundled desktop features were not exercised by this test.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The search regression uses a real 201-page PDF through Poppler with a guarded converter that rejects oversized extraction batches. It verifies matches and sparse pages across batch boundaries, continuation offsets, a non-first-page range, and exact total counts after the snippet limit. It also checks converter counts near the cache's page limit to catch repeated extraction caused by eviction.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The source includes synthetic prose/table, scanned, mixed text/image and rotated PDF fixtures and tests against the real Cordis tool registry, filesystem and attachment store. The model capability lookup is controlled in these integration tests; no paid model calls are made.

Install the native dependencies above, then install the pinned test-only npm dependencies:

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run check
npm run test:package
```

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：Page reads reuse cached text and image counts across overlapping ranges and layout switches. Only missing pages launch converters, in batches of at most 100 pages. Each document retains at most 200 text pages across both modes and 4,194,304 text characters (up to 8 MiB of UTF-16 character storage, excluding object overhead), evicting the least recently used pages. Image counts retain one number per physical page, bounded by the 2,000-page document limit. Source fingerprint checks and filesystem permission checks remain in place on every tool call.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：The package check creates a tarball, checks its exact file list, and runs the integration suite against the unpacked package. `npm test` runs against source. To test an existing Harness installation instead, set `DSH_RUNTIME` to that installation's package root. GitHub Actions runs the package suite on Linux with Node 22 and 24, and on macOS with Node 24. Additional Linux Node 24 lanes test Harness `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.1-alpha.2`, `0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.5`, and `0.2.2-alpha.2`; the default dependency set remains `0.2.0-rc.2`. An OS test run checks the plugin and native tools, not a packaged desktop GUI.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：Tests use a fresh temporary Harness home and never modify the user's conversations or credentials. They follow the plugin's normal Tesseract discovery (`~/.local/share/dsh-pdf-reader/tesseract`, then `PATH`) unless `DSH_PDF_TEST_TESSERACT` selects an absolute executable path. The English and Simplified Chinese data must both be installed.

For the real CLI lifecycle check, use a separately installed exact Harness version (not a desktop shell shim):

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：```sh
DSH_CLI=/absolute/path/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js npm run test:profile
```

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：It packs this checkout, creates a new temporary `DSH_HOME`, uses the official plugin add/remove commands, boots a minimal profile with real host services, checks tool visibility and text extraction, then verifies uninstall and removes its test home. It never writes a normal DSH profile and does not require model credentials. A valid installation of pnpm and Poppler must be available. `DSH_PROFILE_EVIDENCE=/absolute/path/report.json` saves the bounded result.

dsh-pdf-reader README · Verification：This establishes document-processing behavior, not an end-to-end model accuracy benchmark. To measure model gains, hold model, prompts and decoding settings fixed and compare existing attachment handling, these tools, and manually verified evidence on the same PDFs. Use `evaluation.json` in the source directory as the starting rubric.
